What does JABS annotation look like?

Your course VM comes with JABS already installed - the hands-on annotation exercise happens there, for real. This page previews that workflow first: labeling frames, training, and reviewing predictions inside the desktop app, so you know what to expect before you sit down at the VM.

This is a hand-built mockup of the JABS window, not a live screenshot - for the authoritative, always-current reference, see the JABS documentation's GUI and Labeling pages.

Where this fits in the live demo
This page is a preview - on your course VM, JABS is already installed and you'll do this labeling loop for real. The notebook picks up after that GUI work is done: it calls jabs-classify train on a training file already exported from the GUI above, then jabs-classify classify to run that classifier on new sessions, live, in the notebook. Head back to “Train and Classify - Live” in jabs-demo.ipynb to see that step. If the k-fold report above confused you, see “A Note on the JABS GUI’s Own Training Report” right after the classifier metrics in that same notebook for the full explanation.
